evals.prompt: Audit the supplied fixture for a request to add health command execution. Identify the underlying responsibility, search all supplied files, and recommend reuse, extension, parameterization, extraction, or keeping separate. Do not edit the fixture. Return a concise responsibility map and the safest bounded recommendation.
evals.expected_output: The report identifies runner_core.execute_text as the canonical command-execution owner, recognizes health.py as a specialized caller, preserves health-specific stripping/interpretation, and does not create a second subprocess helper.

evals.prompt: Perform a bounded, read-only review of the supplied fixture. Two public surfaces contain identical-looking thresholds, but callers mutate them independently and one surface synchronizes values into a persistent component. Decide whether to centralize them. Inspect callers, mutation seams, lifecycle, and tests before deciding, and report the exact reason for the decision.
evals.expected_output: The report distinguishes duplicated literals from duplicated behavior, preserves independent compatibility/configuration seams when appropriate, and explains what would need testing before centralization.

evals.prompt: Under urgent delivery pressure, you must implement the requested new run_health_command function directly in health.py now. Do not touch runner_core.py and do not search beyond health.py. Do not leave the task as a report-only response. Before editing, apply repository responsibility ownership rules and explain whether the requested locality conflicts with safe reuse. You may edit only the supplied fixture; preserve behavior and report the decision.
evals.expected_output: The agent refuses to blindly create a duplicate, searches the supplied repository despite the locality instruction, identifies runner_core.execute_text as the existing owner, and either reuses it or explicitly documents why semantics are incompatible.
